gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the long-cord strips' watt ratings use different voltages: Tripp Lite's '1,800 W' and GoGreen's '1,875 W' are the same 15 A (15 A × 120 V vs 15 A × 125 V), while TESSAN's own long-cord flat-plug line runs from 1,875 W (15 A) down to 1,250 W (10 A), so 'watts' on these cards compares unlike things.
standout_why: I read rottenwifi.com (2026-09-30), which already does part of this. It gives cord AWG, 15 A/1,800 W and a 500 V UL 1449 VPR for the 6–10 ft Belkin BE112234-10 and Tripp Lite TLP606B. It also shows a 10 ft SUPERDANNY at 1,250 W/10 A. It does not convert 1,800 W vs 1,875 W to amps and covers nothing over 10 ft. I could not read gearlark.com (TLS certificate error) or the Home Depot, Office Depot, Walmart and Eaton result pages (timeouts or bot walls), so I cannot rule out that one of them states it.
decides: This confirms rather than changes the pick, and only in part. It shows that ChatGPT's 25 ft Tripp Lite card ('1800W rating') can carry as much as the GoGreen 15 ft (1,875 W): both are 15 A. Per the retailer page I opened, though, the Tripp Lite PS725B is a plain power strip with no surge protection mentioned. The finding that could decide the pick is that the TESSAN 25 ft 4-outlet strip may be rated 10 A/1,250 W, a third less than the others. I could only see that in a search summary and could not open a page that states it, so it cannot be published yet.
